writeup: TIC 355734358 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry with an orbital period of 4.485 days and a primary eclipse depth of 6.98 percent dimming. The detection has a high signal-to-noise ratio of 173.5 in the automated transit search, and pixel-level analysis yields a confirmation signal of 16.2. However, the star does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and two data quality issues warrant caution. First, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the initially measured period was half the true value - the corrected period listed here accounts for this signature. Second, the pixel centroid lies only 0.030 pixels from a nearby bright star, within TESS's systematic uncertainty, so we cannot confidently rule out contamination from that neighbor. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate merits further investigation to clarify its nature and separate it from nearby sources.
